quick_start.title: Quick start
quick_start.summary: Connect, sync, complete costs, and validate in shadow mode before real operations.
quick_start.purpose: Create a diagnosable, approvable, and auditable GMV MAX workspace.
quick_start.when: First use, store changes, or TikTok account reauthorization.
quick_start.data: A valid connection, store binding, campaigns, products, creatives, and at least one complete report day.
quick_start.logic: Readiness is checked across connection, data, profit model, and historical validation. Missing layers never appear executable.

steps.1: Connect TikTok and verify account, store, and campaign permissions.
steps.2: Sync data, then sync products and creatives.
steps.3: Complete price, costs, and refund assumptions for the current product.
steps.4: Review diagnosis and shadow suggestions before enabling approval permissions.

quick_start.result: The workspace shows real objects, profit floors, issues, and valid action routes.
quick_start.risk: Do not approve budget or ROI changes with incomplete costs or stale data.

data_sync.title: Data sync
data_sync.summary: Understand full sync, catalog sync, and data freshness.
data_sync.purpose: Refresh platform campaigns, reports, products, creatives, and authorization for local decisions.
data_sync.when: Before daily review, after platform edits, or after stale or interrupted data.
data_sync.data: A valid platform connection and read permissions. Complete days use the store timezone.
data_sync.logic: Full sync processes stores, campaigns, reports, realtime data, and SOP. Catalog sync processes products, creatives, authorization, and SOP.

steps.1: Confirm the store and statistic dates.
steps.2: Start the required sync and wait for blocking progress to finish.
steps.3: On failure, inspect the exact phase and avoid concurrent retries.
steps.4: Verify the latest delivery date and data source.

data_sync.result: SOP, creative grades, and profit diagnosis are recalculated with current evidence.
data_sync.risk: Sync time is not the latest delivery date, and missing dates are not zero values.

overview.title: Business overview
overview.summary: Review risk, profit, and pending actions before opening details.
overview.purpose: See spend, GMV, orders, ROI, profit protection, and approvals across stores and campaigns.
overview.when: Daily review, anomaly checks, and management summaries.
overview.data: Campaign reports, cost models, policy settings, and sync state.
overview.logic: Metrics aggregate the selected stores, types, and complete dates. Profit conclusions require sufficient cost coverage.

steps.1: Select store, type, and date range.
steps.2: Check profit protection, freshness, and alerts.
steps.4: Sync again after treatment and verify its state.

overview.result: You can identify the first object to handle and why.
overview.risk: Aggregates cannot replace product-level budget or intraday spend.

sop.title: 30-day SOP
sop.summary: New products, mature products, and LIVE use different tracks and gates.
sop.purpose: Turn operations into stages, issues, daily tasks, one recommended action, and observation locks.
sop.when: Product launch, mature recovery, LIVE support, and controlled scaling.
sop.data: Product age, delivery days, orders, profit, creatives, LIVE, and supplemental metrics.
sop.logic: Dates only set the earliest phase. Evidence gates advancement. Dormant or stale mature products enter recovery diagnosis.

steps.1: Confirm product, campaign, store, and track in the object picker.
steps.3: Change one variable and observe three delivery days.
steps.4: Advance only with profitable days, complete data, and creative supply.

sop.result: Each instance has a clear phase, blocker, route, and completion rule.
sop.risk: Track overrides need a reason. Never run mature products through new-product cold start.

campaigns.title: Campaigns
campaigns.summary: Inspect budget, target ROI, pacing, learning phase, and protection state.
campaigns.purpose: Locate campaign health and open its evidence and pending actions.
campaigns.when: Spend anomalies, ROI changes, disabled campaigns, or controlled scaling.
campaigns.data: Campaign settings, reports, intraday spend in store timezone, policy, and profit floor.
campaigns.logic: Pacing compares the current period with valid historical days. Campaign totals never impersonate missing product metrics.

steps.1: Filter and open the target campaign.
steps.2: Verify status, budget, target ROI, and evidence dates.
steps.4: Use approvals for any write action.

campaigns.result: Each issue points to the exact campaign and variable.
campaigns.risk: Mature recovery cannot immediately enable Auto Budget, Max Delivery, or budget increases.

growth.title: Growth and learning
growth.summary: Identify scalable, testing, and declining products from evidence.
growth.purpose: Evaluate lifecycle, allocation, action outcomes, and the next growth opportunity.
growth.when: After stable profit, at a mature growth ceiling, or when comparing product contribution.
growth.data: Product spend, GMV, orders, ROI, profit, creative count, and action outcomes.
growth.logic: Protect verified profit and Winners first, then allocate tests and scaling from evidence.

steps.1: Sort products by profit or growth potential.
steps.2: Open a product and review recent and historical evidence.
steps.3: Confirm cost coverage and creative supply.

growth.result: Growth actions include a product, evidence period, and expected profit impact.
growth.risk: Projections are not platform guarantees and require delivery-day validation.

rules.title: Policy settings
rules.summary: Set profit-first, balanced-growth, or GMV-growth protection boundaries.
rules.purpose: Define ROI gates, test budgets, exploration share, and write permissions.
rules.when: Campaign initialization, goal changes, or enabling automated SOP drafts.
rules.data: Profit floor, target CPA, creative pool size, and risk preference.
rules.logic: Policies change recommendation boundaries. Writes still require permission, approval, a single-variable lock, and platform verification.

steps.1: Choose a policy preset that matches the business goal.
steps.2: Verify minimum ROI, target CPA, and creative test budget.
steps.3: Enable budget, ROI, status, or creative permissions individually.
steps.4: Run shadow validation before automated drafts.

rules.result: Decisions use explicit and auditable current policy values.
rules.risk: Do not change several thresholds together because attribution becomes impossible.

creatives.title: Creative workspace
creatives.summary: Manage Winner, sustainable, pending-validation, and exclusion-candidate videos.
creatives.purpose: Review previews and evidence, then create heat, exclusion, or rotation approval actions.
creatives.when: Creative supply is low, ROI declines, scaling needs supply, or waste must be removed.
creatives.data: Video identity, impressions, clicks, CTR, orders, GMV, spend, ROI, depth, and authorization.
creatives.logic: S is a profitable Winner, A has sustainable conversions, B has exposure awaiting proof, and C has weak click and conversion. Profitable historical Winners are protected.

steps.1: Filter by grade and sort by profit, ROI, or freshness.
steps.2: Open the video preview and verify identity and evidence.
steps.3: For heat, set budget, start, and end time. Before exclusion, verify Winner protection.
steps.4: Submit approval and observe actual profit after execution.

creatives.result: Every creative action has an object, schedule, budget, reason, and audit trail.
creatives.risk: Do not heat or exclude with insufficient evidence. Help never creates drafts or platform writes.

profit.title: Profit protection
profit.summary: Calculate break-even ROI and the effective floor from complete costs.
profit.purpose: Prevent GMV or platform ROI from hiding purchasing, logistics, commission, and return losses.
profit.when: Product setup, cost or currency changes, or a loss warning.
profit.data: Price, purchase, first mile, last mile, storage, commissions, return rate, and return loss.
profit.logic: Break-even ROI is revenue divided by allowable ad cost. The effective floor adds the current policy safety margin.

steps.1: Filter the current product and verify currency.
steps.3: Save and review coverage and the effective floor.

profit.result: Budget, ROI, and creative suggestions respect real profit boundaries.
profit.risk: Incorrect currency, refunds, or default costs directly change profit decisions.

actions.title: Approval actions
actions.summary: Review before and after values, evidence, and risk before a real platform write.
actions.purpose: Approve budget, target ROI, status, and creative operations with execution and rollback records.
actions.when: After SOP or the optimizer creates a pending recommendation.
actions.data: Current and proposed values, evidence dates, profit floor, orders, permissions, and observation lock.
actions.logic: Only approval invokes a real write. Platform acceptance and state verification are separate. Unknown state requires verification before retry.

steps.1: Filter the campaign and pending status.
steps.2: Check variable, change size, profit floor, and dates.
steps.4: Review request ID, verification, and observation result.

actions.result: Every platform change has approval, request, result, and rollback eligibility.
actions.risk: Never retry an uncertain write directly because it may apply twice.

audit.title: Connection and audit
audit.summary: Track capabilities, requests, failures, and real execution state.
audit.purpose: Confirm available read and write capabilities and trace each operation.
audit.when: Execution failure, permission changes, state mismatch, or review.
audit.data: Connection capability, audit action, request ID, error, and timestamps.
audit.logic: Audit distinguishes started, accepted, verified, failed, and uncertain states.

steps.1: Filter by campaign, state, or action.
steps.2: Inspect request ID and error details.
steps.3: Verify uncertain actions on the platform first.
steps.4: Retry only if no write occurred, or roll back when eligible.

audit.result: The record shows what the system did, what the platform returned, and the final state.
audit.risk: Accepted without verification does not prove that the setting took effect.

metrics.title: Metrics and formulas
metrics.summary: Understand ROI, Net ROI, Live Score, and mature-product health coverage.
metrics.purpose: Use consistent definitions and avoid treating missing values as zero.
metrics.when: Reviewing diagnosis, comparing reports, or explaining a blocked phase.
metrics.data: Spend, GMV, refunds, orders, clicks, impressions, LIVE funnel, and historical baselines.
metrics.logic: ROI=GMV/spend; Net GMV=GMV-refunds; Net ROI=Net GMV/spend. Live Score weights click 30%, order 40%, paid 20%, and stay 10%.

steps.1: Confirm statistic date, store timezone, and currency.
steps.2: Separate missing dates, zero-spend days, and complete delivery days.
steps.3: Review metric source and update time.
steps.4: Interpret against the current policy, not a universal fixed value.

metrics.result: Metrics can be recalculated and traced to a source.
metrics.risk: Zero-spend days are not profitable days. Mature coverage below 80% allows diagnosis only.

execution.title: Real execution and rollback
execution.summary: Understand approval, acceptance, verification, observation, and rollback.
execution.purpose: Ensure recommendations produce real controlled actions without duplicate writes or variable interference.
execution.when: Before approval, after failure, after performance decline, or before restoration.
execution.data: Approval record, request ID, platform response, before and after values, and three delivery days.
execution.logic: Only one variable executes at a time. Other variables lock for three delivery days, then the system holds or proposes rollback from profit evidence.

steps.1: Confirm the connection supports the intended write.
steps.2: Approve one action and record the platform request.
steps.3: Sync and verify actual platform state.
steps.4: After observation, hold or approve an eligible rollback.

execution.result: Real actions form an auditable loop from recommendation to outcome.
execution.risk: External Seller Center actions need actual value, date, and evidence before completion.

issues.title: Issue knowledge base
issues.summary: Covers every SOP blocker, operation anomaly, sync failure, and write failure.
issues.purpose: Explain the judgment, values, resolution route, and completion rule.
issues.when: An SOP issue appears or the next action is unclear.
issues.data: Issue code, evidence, policy target, source, and action status for the current object.
issues.logic: Issues are ordered as must fix, recommended, observing, and resolved. One code always maps to one resolution contract.

steps.1: Open an issue from the current list or search.
steps.2: Read the cause, values, and completion rule.
steps.3: Follow the in-app or Seller Center steps.
steps.4: Sync new evidence and let the system verify completion.

issues.result: Every issue has an actionable resolution instead of a generic hint.
issues.risk: Wait-for-data issues cannot be completed manually and require real evidence.
